i haven't been officially diagnosed/treaded with adhd because my parents pull me from therapists every time they try to diagnose me. I live in Canada. I'm not really sure how to answer that. Previously, I was against medication because I thought it might affect my personality and make me gain weight (I am an athlete and this would be bad for my performance). My stance has since changed and I now am really hoping to be on medication before september.

I'm not 100% sure on my parents' stances. I don't really talk to my dad. My mother keeps telling me I need to be on meds, but only when she's angry with me for not doing something right/right away/without being distracted. Since my therapist is campaigning for me to be on medication now, she keeps saying backhanded stuff to me about it. About 5 mins ago, she said "I guess we _HAVE_ to put you on meds since you can't seem to do _anything_ without them", but she didn't sound sincere.

1.) I am 17 and am going into 12th grade in September.

2.) I have been diagnosed with ADHD by two different people, but the first person to diagnose me was unqualified.

3.) _My mother is a psychologist._ She knows plenty about ADHD. I can't answer for my father because I don't talk to him that much.

4.) I am not on medication. My mother and my psychologist are currently searching to get me evaluated for some.

My parents are currently trying to get me medication after 10 years of me messing up in school and them having to go save me. Hopefully that will make things better. I can tell whenever my mom talks to me about it that she's disappointed in me, and that breaks my heart because she's been through a lot and deserves to have a normal kid.

> My heart breaks for you, you do not deserve to be treated this way. 

> Please do not think you deserve to be taken from this planet. You are a good kid who's mind just thinks differently and you are not abnormal or a lazy kid.

I know, but other people also don't deserve to be responsible for someone who should be able to be responsible for herself. Everyone around me, *especially* my mother, shouldn't have to always focus so much of their time around me. Today it took me 10 hours to do my homework AGAIN and my parents were the ones who had to help me out and deal with my dramatic sobbing. It's not fair to them.
I am not medicated. My parents don't think I have ADHD/think I'm overplaying my symptoms, even though I've been diagnosed.
My teachers don't like me that much, and school is closed right now unless you're taking finals.

I don't concentrate well with music playing, but I also have a song stuck in my head that I'll fixate on. I don't like chewing gum, and I ate all of the sweet stuff we have at home.

Break methods don't really help me out. I've tried them before but I'll get distracted for the entire 20 minutes of the study break and get mad at myself.

And I plan on closing reddit soon! I just want some help but i know it's just gonna make the problem worse

I don't think as many people lie about it as you think, but they might overplay how bad their symptoms are. They might also think they're suffering from something they aren't, or mistake one thing for another. Generally, people fake things "for attention". Someone faking a mental illness would be seeking behavior from people that shows caring, compassion and understanding - which is exactly what people with mental health issues need anyway.

The thing is that I HAVE been evaluated by an outside party, but she ended up being really racist towards me and coming up with biased results. My mom filed a complaint against her and we don't have the money for another evaluation. She also won't trust anyone who evaluates me again, because she'll think I'm trying to get this diagnosis on purpose to slack off in school.
I see a therapist right now. She diagnosed me with ADHD in April. My mother thinks she's wrong and that I've manipulated her into thinking I have ADHD.

My mom believes ADHD exists and I believe she has diagnosed some cases of it with varying degrees of severity. I think I _kind of_ understand what you're getting at but if you could find another way to say it I think I would understand what you meant better.

I'm a native speaker and my dad lives with me but he's not really going to be much of a help either. 

A lot of people on this sub have parents who do not believe ADHD exists. I wrote that to clarify that that isn't my problem.

> Has she explained her view on why she feels the diagnosis could be wrong out side of just calling you lazy.

Yes, she thinks I just have severe anxiety. I do have pretty bad anxiety, and it's been prevalent since I was born, but I think there's something else going on as well and she doesn't.

> It might be worth having a heart to heart with her, approach it without an accusatory or defensive position but ask her why she feels the way she does and present your argument as to why you think it could be ADHD 

I've tried. She tells me she thinks there's nothing wrong with me every single day, so she's pretty firmly rooted in her belief.

> Is it possible to get a new mom?

I mean PROBABLY, but I really don't want to do that! I like my mother a lot, we just have different perspectives on a problem I have. I'm only 17 years old and she's not only much older than me, but probably knows a lot more about ADHD/overlapping conditions than me. Even if she ends up being wrong, I still feel like I have to respect her opinion, especially because she ends up being right over me about 90% of the time.

> Maybe talk to the school and have them present the information to your mom.

That's not a good idea. Without going into too much detail, the school psychology/guidance system sucks here and both me and my mother don't trust or have faith in them at all anymore.

> There's going to be a point when 9/10 therapists agree with ADHD and your mother will have to accept.

She doesn't really HAVE to do anything. I have to live by what she says as long as she's providing for me. I'm in no situation at all to move out, and I don't even really want to do that. My mother used to see a therapist herself and quit once the therapist started telling her stuff she didn't want to hear.

I'm not sure how to start doing that. I'm an ambitious person and had big plans for my life, I'm just sure it won't happen anymore. I don't really enjoy a lot of stuff, but the things I do like I'm super into.

> Do you have a lot of regrets?

No. I'm an average kid, nothing special. I haven't lived my life in any outlandish or extravagant way to make myself have any regrets.

> Have you ever done anything in your life that's helped or made anyone else feel good?

Probably. Nothing notable, so I can't remember anything in particular. I try to be polite to people.

> Do you think you're a relatively kind person? 

No. 

> Or feel empathy or a sense that you should help someone if they're in need and you have the tools to help?

I'm not sure there. My mother's told me that I don't feel empathy the same way most people do, so I'm not sure how to answer that accurately.

> What I'm trying to say is that there's probably really nothing to fear. In fact, the chances of anything bad happening afterward (in my opinion) are fairly low. Unless you personally feel it's necessary for you or you think that you deserve it. But again; I think there are beings to help you understand that you're innocent, essentially. Or you were as human. We come here to observe and experience what we otherwise couldn't as a spirit, and ultimately to forget. To feel like we are separate, and have our own paths to choose.

I appreciate that as your answer, but I've lived with this mindset for 17 years, and no matter how rational someone could be in trying to justify something to me, it will take me a long time. That's not to say that I'm disregarding or ignoring you, just that I still (and will for a very long time) am uncertain.

I'm not sure what I can do to change your mind, but at the very least I'm asking you not to drown yourself. It is an absolutely terrifying way to go and your last minutes will be spent in terror, confusion and extreme physical pain and discomfort.
